note:
**The 1861 round, Western Terrace.** Extra Parochial, Nottingham, schedules 161 to 171, read from the enumerator's page by A. Hagues. **The record held four people in 1861 before this.**

## The houses are placed by arithmetic, not by guesswork

The 1861 enumerator walks Western Terrace in the same order as the 1871 one, household for household, **exactly twenty schedule numbers earlier**. Three of the households are demonstrably the same people, ten years apart:

| 1861 | 1871 | |
|---|---|---|
| 162 **John Wood**, 63 | 142 **John Wood**, 71 | the same man |
| 163 Alexander Alliott, 55, with **Mary**, 51 | 143 **Mary Alliott**, 61, now widowed | the same woman, the same house |
| 166 **James Roger Allen**, 67 | 146 **James R Allen**, 77 | the same man |

Mary Alliott heads 1 Western Terrace in 1871 and her son **James B Alliott** is there in 1881, so the anchor holds over three rounds. James Roger Allen sits four houses along in both 1861 and 1871. With the offset fixed at twenty in three places, **schedules 163 to 168 are 1 to 6 Western Terrace** and no inference is needed beyond the arithmetic.

## What is still not explained

**Two households stand ahead of number 1 and are left unfiled.** Schedule 161 - whose head is on the sheet before this one, so only four servants show - and schedule 162, John Wood. The same thing happens in 1871, where three households precede number 1 in exactly this way and John Wood is again the last of them. Two enumerators a decade apart both put houses on Western Terrace before its first number, so the explanation belongs to the street and not to the clerk. See [[three-western-terrace-households-before-number-one]].

## Who is here

**Alexander Alliott**, engineer and lace manufacturer, at 1 Western Terrace with nine in the house including his wife's mother **Elizabeth Bingham at 86**, living independent. He is dead by 1871 and Mary keeps the house.

**William Milton**, widower, **Perpetual Curate of New Radford**, at 2 with four young children, a governess and three servants.

**Edward Manlove**, manufacturing engineer, at 6, with a son of 21 already in the same trade and a baby of ten months.

**John Lawson Thackeray** on Derby Road at schedule 169 - **cotton doubler and magistrate**, born at Saddleworth in Yorkshire, a widower or with his wife away, four servants and a nursemaid for three small children. Unfiled: the page gives Derby Road and no number.

## Left out

**Schedule 170 is the Barracks** - Alfred Mason the canteen keeper, his wife and seven children, three of them born at the Barracks. It is not The Park and is not entered, but the household is named here so it is not lost.

**Schedule 171 is entered as "Park" with no house named** - Charles S Hadden, hosiery manufacturer, and five of his family. It is in the record, unfiled.

**The page totals check.** The first sheet says 3 houses, 4 males and 21 females, and holds 25 people; the second says 4 houses, 9 males and 16 females, and holds 25. Both add up.
